newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Trade and technicals.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT MARKET OUTLOOK - Trade and technicals.

text.p: August trade data and technical factors are likely to generate the lion's share of credit market price action on Friday, analysts predicted.

On Thursday the market pierced a key resistance level, suggesting further chart-based gains may be forthcoming. And while trade figures are usually of more interest to the currency markets, the size of July's mammoth trade shortfall clearly has the Treasury market on its toes as well.
"I think you need to watch that trade number at 0830 (EDT) on Friday a little more closely than we've been trained to watch it," said Patrick Dimick, treasury analyst at CS First Boston.
"If it creeps above $12 billion instead of shrinking the dollar would almost surely give up some of its recent gains and bonds would come under pressure," he added.
The trade gap for goods and services is expected to shrink to $8.5 billion from an eight-and-a-half year high of $11.68 billion in July, according to a Reuters poll of economists.
Imports rose by a modest 1.2 percent in July.
Apart from the trade numbers, analysts said that technical factors would dominate the otherwise data-sparse Friday session.
On Thursday, the December T-bond futures contract closed at 111-04/32, above a key resistance level of 110-26/32, which had acted as a ceiling to the market for over a week.
"I think that that's a good technical signal that could generate some additional buying in the overnight session," said Dimick. "I think that will be an important story."
If the gap does narrow signficantly the dollar should add to its recent strength and bonds would likely follow suit. But some analysts said the downside risks may outweigh the upside potential.

"My feeling is that the dollar is more liable to be hurt by a wider deficit than it's going to be helped by a narrower one," said Richard Koss, international economist at MFR Inc. "In terms of the bond market impact, the composition becomes important."
Exports dropped by a hefty 3.6 percent in July and are expected to rebound in the August report.
The benchmark 6.75 percent ended the day up 24/32 at 99-11/32 to yield 6.80 percent. The federal funds rate is expected to open between 5-1/8 and 5-3/16 on Friday.
